LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 3.1.3 POLITE LANGUAGE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 3.1.3 Polite language
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 3.1.3 Polite language, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use polite language? 2. When do we use polite language?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (listening and speaking) 3.1.3 Polite language together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: signing skills as learner signs words used to request, apologise and appreciate.

• Creativity and Imagination:Exploration -imagination and originality as learner engages in signed dialogue using polite language

in class.

Values:
• Respect:Humility as learner uses polite language to interact, request, apologize and appreciate others in daily life.

• Love:Caring as learner purposes to maintain good relations with those around by using polite language.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Family conflicts under citizenship education is avoided by the learner with the awareness of using polite language to maintain good

social relations.
